title: Cell-7 Heading with Displayed Quotation

illustrates.quote: Follow a cell-7 heading by accompanying text, including lists, on the next line. (See Sample 4-4: Cell-7 Heading with Displayed Quotation on page 4-19.)

blocks.text: Striking the proper balance between freedom for the individual and the rights of society as a whole is similarly difficult—and vital. Abraham Lincoln once stated democracy's problem in these words:

braille.notes: Numbering begins at 6 in the source (lines 1-5 of this braille page precede the excerpt). Lines 6-10 the lead-in paragraph (2-cell indent); line 11 blank; line 12 the cell-7 heading 'PRIMARY Sources' (whole-word cap on 'PRIMARY', single-cap on 'Sources' -- NOT full caps on both words), indented 8 cells rather than the usual 6 (see uncertain); lines 13-15 the quotation body at a 2-cell indent; lines 16-17 the attribution, indented 6 cells; line 18 blank; line 19 the resuming sentence, ending '444'.

uncertain: The heading 'PRIMARY Sources' is indented 8 cells rather than a plain 6; read as 'cell-7 (6) plus the displayed quotation's own 2-cell margin shift' (6+2=8) rather than a different heading level, because the sample's own title names it a cell-7 heading and the quotation body lines around it are consistently shifted by the same 2 cells -- though the attribution lines (16-17) are back at a plain 6-cell indent, not 8, so the '+2 applies to the heading line too' reading is not fully consistent and was not cross-checked against another worked example of a heading nested inside a displayed quotation elsewhere in Formats (this section has none).
resolution: braille.lines agree. Text resolved to "PRIMARY Sources" (matching run B): the braille's double-comma indicator on "prim>y" (whole-word caps) but single-comma on "s\rces" (initial cap only) shows print reads "PRIMARY Sources", not run A's "Primary Sources" (which the same braille contradicts). `print.blocks` kept as run A's 5-block split (quotation body and citation as two separate `other` blocks, matching their different braille indents) rather than run B's single merged block -- a documentation-only choice since `other` blocks are excluded from modeling either way.
